T01.rationale: Colkitt built Ambient Finance (ex-Citadel quant); Sagurton ran digital-asset sales at Jump Crypto; engineering comes from Douro Labs, the team behind Pyth and Pythnet. Outcomes of Ambient were not established from these sources.

T03.rationale: 9 human committers across the two public repos in the 90 days to listing, several from Douro Labs; core development depends on one outside firm, and no security, BD or ops leads are named.

T04.rationale: In-house (Douro Labs) engineers ship public changes to a Firedancer fork (zones, validator manager, fixed inflation) and an original Sessions standard; the underlying client is Jump's work, not theirs.

T05.rationale: No enforcement or misconduct found; public criticism concerns pricing (the $1B-FDV presale called 'extractive', cancelled within two days) and raising on forked code, not conduct.

T07.rationale: Validators are hand-picked by a genesis authority and clustered in one zone; there is no token-holder governance and the DAO roadmap has no dates.

notes: missing: Foundation and launch-liquidity wallet addresses (21.76% + 6.5% unlocked at TGE) and any treasury reporting; fogo.io docs could not be accessed in this review

T09.rationale: Seed led by Distributed Global with CMS Holdings, then an Echo community round (Cobie, Kain Warwick, Larry Cermak, ~3,200 investors) and a Binance Wallet sale; crypto-native funds and angels, no record of support through a down cycle established.

notes: Dec 11 tokenomics (FOGO-01/02) and launch tokenomics (FOGO-09/11) differ: institutional 8.77% to 12.06%, Foundation ~30.4% to 21.76% + 6.5% launch liquidity, and the 2% presale cancelled on 13 Dec was redirected to an airdrop, while a separate 2% was sold a month later in the Binance Wallet Prime Sale ($7M at $0.035 vs the presale's $0.10). Recorded as claims C1-C3.

P01.rationale: Low-latency on-chain trading is a real need, but Fogo's only usage so far is testnet activity rewarded with Flames points that convert into the airdrop.

P02.rationale: Public mainnet went live 13–15 Jan 2026, days before listing; Sessions is still a 'developer preview' and zone rotation and open validator entry are not live.

P03.rationale: Client is a declared fork of Firedancer with meaningful changes (multi-local zones, validator manager, fixed 2% inflation, Sessions instruction).

P04.rationale: Speed comes from co-locating validators in one data centre in Asia with a single client; a global fallback is described but its trigger is undocumented and untested on mainnet.

P05.rationale: Depends on upstream Firedancer (Jump) as its only client, Wormhole as the sole official bridge for USDC/ETH/SOL, Douro Labs for engineering and one data centre for block production.

P08.rationale: Testnet and mainnet were planned for H1 2025; testnet shipped July 2025 and mainnet January 2026, about six months late.

P09.rationale: Validator client and Sessions programs are public under Apache 2.0; reproducible builds against mainnet binaries are not documented.

notes: missing: docs.fogo.io and the litepaper could not be accessed in this review; need technical specs for zone rotation, fallback and validator admission
fogo.io and docs.fogo.io could not be fetched in this review (access not granted), so official docs, the litepaper, treasury addresses and the published vesting addresses were not read directly.

S02.rationale: The only audit found covers upstream Firedancer v0.1 for Jump (2 highs, Agave runtime out of scope); Fogo's own modifications and the Sessions programs have no public audit.

notes: No upgrade timelock is documented. Protocol changes ship as client releases adopted by a curated validator set (FOGO-17, FOGO-20). Ask: notice period before upgrades, and who controls the Sessions programs' upgrade authority.

S05.rationale: A genesis authority curates the validator set, and protocol changes ship as client releases from the Foundation-funded team; no on-chain timelock or independent signer set is documented.

S06.rationale: Native token with no mint key; issuance is a fixed 2% a year set in the client. Supply is not fixed, and the BSC token used for the Prime Sale was not checked.
notes: The FOGO sold in the Prime Sale was subscribed on BSC (FOGO-08). The mint authority and bridge for any BSC representation were not checked; RF01 is set from the native token only.
No public bug bounty was found for Fogo or Fogo Sessions.
missing: production history; mainnet was 0–2 days old at as_of, so no incident record exists to judge
missing: which oracle setups the launch DeFi apps use; native Pyth integration is claimed (FOGO-06) but not verified

S10.rationale: USDC, ETH and SOL reach Fogo only through Wormhole, its official native bridge; an established bridge, but all external liquidity sits behind it.

K01.rationale: FOGO pays gas and secures the chain through staking, rewarded by 2% fixed inflation; no fee share, buyback or burn is documented.

notes: Top-holder concentration not established. At TGE the Foundation controls 21.76% plus 6.5% launch liquidity, about 78% of the 36.26% unlocked supply (FOGO-09). Needs labelled holder data from the Fogo explorer; locked allocations' custody (vesting contracts or custodian) is not documented.

Price, market cap, FDV, 24h volume, depth and spread at listing are not set. Trading opened on 15 Jan 2026; no pre-listing exchange snapshot or listing-day price published on or before that date was found. The only priced reference is the Binance Wallet Prime Sale on 13 Jan: $0.035/FOGO, about $350M FDV on 10B supply (FOGO-07, FOGO-08). The Echo round was $8M at a $100M valuation (FOGO-01). M01, M02, M04, M08, K06, K07, B04 are therefore unscored.

K09.rationale: Allocations changed between the 11 Dec tokenomics and launch (institutional 8.77% to 12.06%, Foundation 30.38% to 21.76% + 6.5% launch liquidity) and no vesting contract addresses were found.

K10.rationale: Airdrop goes to testnet game players, bridge-points holders and anyone who sent USDC after 11 Dec, all of which can be farmed; no sybil filtering was disclosed and the checker launched with a display bug.

notes: O01, O02, O03, O07, O10 and TVL are not set: public mainnet was 0–2 days old on 15 Jan 2026 (FOGO-14 says 13 Jan, FOGO-15/16 say 15 Jan).
missing: mainnet activity data; the chain was 0–2 days old at as_of

O09.rationale: About seven launch apps are announced (perps, DEX, lending, LST, launchpad), one of them (Ambient) built by a co-founder; none verified live with users at as_of.

notes: missing: trading history; spot trading started on listing day

M06.rationale: No prior spot venue except Binance Alpha; Binance, OKX, Gate and KuCoin all list it on 15 Jan, reported by one secondary source.

notes: missing: whether perpetual or pre-market futures existed at listing, with OI and funding
missing: on-chain ownership of DEX pools; 6.5% launch-liquidity allocation is Foundation-held (FOGO-09) but its deployment was not verified

M10.rationale: Launches into a market Fogo itself said did not favour high-FDV launches, as a follower among high-performance SVM chains whose speed edge narrows as Solana adopts Firedancer.

notes: B01, B05, B06, B07, B08 not set: no fee revenue yet; Foundation treasury size and burn rate are not published. Funding raised: $5.5M seed + $8M Echo + $7M Prime Sale (FOGO-07).
missing: no fee revenue history; mainnet days old
missing: fee split/burn parameters on Fogo; docs not accessible, no source found
missing: no activity or revenue data yet
missing: dated pre-listing sizing of the on-chain trading / high-performance L1 segment
missing: no share history; mainnet days old

C04.rationale: The only edge is latency from validator co-location and Firedancer; Solana is adopting the same client (~21% of stake), and no retention has been shown.

C05.rationale: Fogo is itself an Apache-licensed fork of open-source Firedancer; no liquidity or integrations are sticky yet.

C06.rationale: 40ms blocks and gasless Sessions set it apart from Solana today, but both are copyable and Solana's Firedancer rollout narrows the gap.

notes: missing: market FDV at listing (only the $0.035 Prime Sale price, ~$350M FDV, FOGO-07) and dated peer valuations

C08.rationale: The incumbent, Solana, is rolling out the same Firedancer client (~21% of stake), which goes straight at Fogo's speed pitch.

C09.rationale: Wormhole is confirmed live by Wormhole; Pyth and the DEX/lending partners are announced but not observed live.

C10.rationale: Adds another SVM L1 to sectors Binance already covers; the Binance Wallet Prime Sale and Alpha launch tie it to Binance's own funnel.

notes: missing: social analytics (engagement, bot share) for dates before 15 Jan 2026
missing: social analytics for dates before 15 Jan 2026
Holder count not available; the token was not distributed until 15 Jan.
missing: user geography of testnet/airdrop recipients

D05.rationale: Disclosed paid content (sponsored CoinGecko explainer), a 50M FOGO Binance marketing allocation and points campaigns run alongside organic interest.

notes: missing: count of external developers or shipped third-party projects beyond announced launch apps
No token-holder governance exists (FOGO-20); not applicable in practice.

D08.rationale: Published tokenomics and explained the presale cancellation, but a month later sold a separate 2% via the Binance Wallet Prime Sale at a third of the cancelled presale's price and revised investor and Foundation shares; no explanation of the revisions was found.

D09.rationale: Informed participants criticised the $1B-FDV presale and the forked-code raise; the switch to an airdrop answered part of it.

D10.rationale: Integrated by Wormhole, backed by CMS and Distributed Global, sold through Binance Wallet and listed the same day by Binance, OKX, Gate and KuCoin.

notes: missing: Fogo Foundation jurisdiction and registry record

L02.rationale: Tokens were sold to ~3,200 Echo investors and to the public via Binance Wallet while a genesis authority controls the validator set; utility is gas and staking.

notes: sanctions_exposure not established: no public wallet screening. Needs the venue's own Chainalysis/TRM screening of the Foundation, launch-liquidity, Prime Sale and team addresses.

L04.rationale: A base layer with no custody or exchange function of its own; the public token sales are the only activity that may need a licence.

L05.rationale: No litigation or enforcement found in news coverage; court and regulator registries were not searched directly.

L06.rationale: Transparent SVM ledger forked from Firedancer; no privacy or obfuscation feature appears in the client or the product description.

notes: missing: front-end geofencing and airdrop-eligibility restrictions

gates.title: Unrestricted mint controlled by a single key
gates.why: Supply can be inflated at will; every other number in the report is conditional on one person's restraint.

gates.title: Sanctions / illicit-finance exposure
gates.why: Listing would create direct regulatory liability for the venue.

gates.title: Core contracts not source-verified
gates.why: Nobody outside the team can see what users are interacting with.

gates.title: Unremediated exploit with user losses
gates.why: Users are owed money; listing would expose new users to the same counterparty.

gates.title: Active enforcement action against the project or founders
gates.why: Outcome could force delisting or freeze assets after listing.

gates.title: Upgradeable contracts with no meaningful timelock
gates.why: Logic can change under users with no time to exit.

gates.title: Extreme holder concentration
gates.why: A handful of wallets can set the price; order books will not absorb their exit.

gates.title: Unlock cliff within 90 days
gates.why: More than a quarter of circulating supply unlocks shortly after a listing window.

gates.title: No independent audit
gates.why: Code holding user funds has never been reviewed by a third party.

gates.title: Material misrepresentation
gates.why: Two or more project claims contradicted by observed data — the reviewer cannot rely on anything self-reported.

gates.title: Security pillar failing
gates.why: Average security score below 1.5/4 — structural rather than one-off weakness.

gates.title: Anonymous team with centralised admin powers
Undisclosed market-maker terms
gates.why: Token loans and call options are where post-listing dumps are engineered.

gates.title: Insider-heavy allocation
gates.why: Team and investors hold more than half of supply.

gates.title: Mercenary TVL
gates.why: Most deposits are paid to be there and will leave when incentives stop.

gates.title: Volume implausible versus depth
gates.why: Daily volume more than 100x the ±2% depth is a common wash-trading signature.

claim.statement: December tokenomics: institutional investors (Distributed Global, CMS Holdings) hold 8.77% of supply
